slice: socket broker transport, manager confinement, sudoers removal, and rollback

target.name: brln-os-hardening-053-pkg-20260810
target.network: loopback-only NAT SSH forward during the gate; original bridged NIC restored afterward

accepted: The manager reached the privileged broker through an AF_UNIX systemd socket as the canonical lightningos UID.
A different local account could not use the socket and direct sudo execution of the broker was unavailable after cutover.

The manager remained healthy with NoNewPrivileges=yes, PrivateDevices=yes, ProtectSystem=strict, empty capability sets, kernel and control-group protections, restricted address families, and the audited syscall deny set.
The legacy manager sudoers file and stale login-enable sudoers file were absent after cutover; the manager had no docker supplementary group.
Docker InvocationID was unchanged through forward cutover and rollback.
The rollback restored the prior manager and broker binaries, manager unit and drop-in, config, sudoers policy, Docker membership, and prior socket state.
Bitcoin, LND, PostgreSQL, Docker, and application data were not copied, deleted, reset, reindexed, or ownership-rewritten by the cutover or rollback.
systemd-analyze security reported overall exposure 2.5 (OK) for the confined manager in this gate.
observations: LND was already in an automatic activating/restart cycle before the privilege gate and remained in that pre-existing condition; the gate did not deliberately restart LND.
The first health probe immediately after manager restart raced startup and triggered automatic rollback as designed. The repeated gate used a bounded readiness loop and passed.
An older root-only rollback bundle from the previous disposable gate was preserved during testing and restored afterward.
